name: seating
title: Seating
description: Seats for a table: random or ordered seating, joining under a checked name, leaving, returning to an existing stack, removing a player and the host's controls, for people and computer players.

facilities.description: Join, leave, lowest free seat, full-table and minimum checks
Random or ordered seat numbers fixed when a game starts
A person who leaves a running game may return to the same seat and stack, or not
Host, who may remove whom, who may start, who may add a computer
Lobby seat list rows for web, Apple and Android clients

text.purpose: `seating` decides who sits where. It holds the seat list of a table (people and computer players), joins a person under a name the guest-identity rule accepts, gives the lowest free seat, refuses a full table or a taken name, lets people leave, lets a person who leaves a running game return to the same seat and stack, removes players, tells who may start the game or add a computer, and fixes seat numbers when a game starts (shuffled, or in the order people sat). It knows nothing about the game played at the table.
text.userInputs: Settings (all optional): `minimumPlayers` (default 2), `maximumPlayers` (default 9, also the number of seats round the table), `seating` (`random` or `order`, default `random`), `returnToStack` (default true) and `hostRemovesPeople` (default false: only computer players can be removed). They map to the house-rules file entries `players.minimum`, `players.maximum`, `players.seating` and `players.return_to_existing_stack_allowed`.
text.integration: Build it once with `createSeating(settings, identity)` from `implementation/server/seating.ts`; `identity` is guest-identity's `createIdentityApi(settings)`, an object with `validName(name)` that has `nameMinLength` and `nameMaxLength` bound. Every operation takes a state and returns a new one. The turn engine keeps the seat state inside the game state and calls `join`, `leave`, `leaveRunning`, `mayReturn`, `remove`, `canStart`, `canAddComputer`, `assign` and `retain`; computer-players calls `join`, `find`, `findByName`, `isFull` and `canAddComputer`; tournament calls `list`, `find` and `people`. Clients use `seatRows` (web `implementation/web/lobby.ts`, Apple `SeatRows.swift`, Android `SeatRows.kt`) to turn a view's players into lobby rows; screens, icons and language text stay with the recipe.
text.infrastructure: No service is deployed. The seat state is part of the game state the room stores; nothing else is kept. No accounts or keys.
text.verification: `node --test tests/web.test.ts` checks settings, joining, names checked by the identity's `validName`, full tables, random and ordered seating (every permutation reachable), returning to a stack, removal rules, start and add-computer checks, retain/compact/ring helpers, seat rows, the runnable consumer and export/import with checksums. `python3 tests/native.py apple` compiles and runs the Swift seat-row checks. `python3 tests/native.py android` is written for Kotlin 2.2 but was not run on the extraction machine (no kotlinc). `authoring/integration.test.ts` (not packaged) runs seating over the real guest-identity sibling.
text.scenarios: Three people and a computer sit in a nine-seat room: numbers 1 to 4 are given in join order, then fixed at random when the host starts. A person leaves a running game and later returns to the same seat and stack; with `returnToStack` off the way back is shut. The host removes a computer player; with `hostRemovesPeople` on, a person too.
text.updates: Patch updates replace files; the seat state shape is `interfaces/seating-state.schema.json` version 1.0.0 and `migration.json` describes export and import of seat assignments as newline-delimited JSON with a checksum per record. Removal deletes the owned sources and the application's imports; the application's stored seat assignments stay in the room's own storage.

agentInstructions: Select `ourapps-ae/seating` once per recipe. Map the recipe's players question to `minimumPlayers` and `maximumPlayers`. Connect the `guest-identity` requirement to the guest-identity component, then connect the provided `seating` to turn-engine (as `seating`), computer-players (as `seating`) and tournament (as `seating`). Seating is `random` unless the house rules say `order`.
developerInstructions: Nothing to supply: no accounts or keys. Pass the same name rule your clients use (guest-identity). If you keep a house-rules file, read the four `players` values into the settings. Use `seatRows` in your lobby screen and keep the text and icons in your own language files. To check it works, run the commands below.

suitability.notes: Pure library; the seat list is part of the room's own stored state, a few hundred bytes.
